gaps.sentence: 'Get out of my way!' the guard snapped. The guard snapped at me ___ out of my way.
gaps.hint: snap at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The order is reported as snapped at me + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'We're leaving here at dawn,' they said. They said they were leaving ___ at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Place adverbs shift with the speaker's perspective: here → there.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Stop the car!' the passenger shouted. The passenger shouted at the driver ___ the car.
gaps.hint: shout at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The command is reported with shout at + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: 'You can rely on me,' she assured me. She assured me that I ___ rely on her.
gaps.explanation: Can backshifts to could after the past reporting verb 'assured'.

gaps.sentence: 'Well done, you've passed!' the examiner said. The examiner ___ me on passing.
'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.
